subject: Acme post-demo: model shortlist & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme post-demo: model shortlist & next steps

Alex — great running through the demo earlier. Quick recap + recommended next steps and a short model shortlist based on what you shared about Acme's primary workloads (customer support summarization + intent classification; 1–2k token prompts, target p95 latency <= 600ms):

Recap:
- Primary goals: improve summary accuracy, reduce hallucinations on product docs, keep latency predictable for UI (p95 <= 600ms).
- Budget guidance: target per-1M-token cost < $25 for inference if possible.
- Data sensitivity: no PII in prompts; audit logs required.

Recommended shortlist (tradeoffs: cost / latency / quality):
1) Mistral-7B-Instruct (quantized FP16) — Best latency/cost balance for short prompts. Expected p95 latency ~150–300ms on our Dedicated 1xA10 config; lower cost, good for classification and summarization with light prompt engineering. Quality: good with few-shot, occasional brevity.
2) LlamaX-13B (8-bit quantized) — Higher quality for nuanced summarization, medium latency (~300–450ms) and moderate cost. Good candidate if accuracy on long-context summaries matters.
3) GPT-NeoX-20B (optimized kernels) — Highest quality on edge cases, but significantly higher cost and latency (~500–800ms). Use only if LlamaX shows regressions on factuality.
4) Hybrid: Mistral-7B for bulk real-time routes + LlamaX-13B as fallback for “high-risk” items (longer docs / legal content).

Attachments: I attached a CSV with the shortlist and expected perf/cost numbers, a sample prompt set we propose for your evals, and a short benchmark summary. Links to the full benchmarks and eval prompt set are below.

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm two models to run a focused POC (we recommend option 1 + 2: Mistral-7B + LlamaX-13B).
- We’ll provision a 2-week eval window with pre-baked prompt set (see attachment) + synthetic/full QA logs.
- Define acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 600ms, ROUGE / BLEU thresholds for summaries, hallucination rate < 2% on a labeled prompt set.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock POC scope (suggest Wed/Thu this week).

Questions for you: can you confirm approximate peak concurrent requests for the UI and whether you need a VPC/private deployment for the POC? Also confirm whether Acme will provide a labeled set for hallucination checks or if we should curate one from your sample docs.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0198

Alex — perfect, thanks for the quick answers. We’ll start the provisioning once you confirm the labeled set share. A couple of implementation/POC details and guardrails so expectations are clear:

Eval plan (2-week):
- Week 1: baseline run using your labeled set + our synthetic stress tests. Collect p50/p95 latency, token cost, and quality metrics (ROUGE-L for summaries, hallucination rate measured against labeled checklist).
- Week 2: prompt tuning + rollout test (A/B) against real traffic sample we’ll replay with your data.

Key metrics we’ll deliver in the eval report:
- Latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95)
- Cost per 1M tokens served (USD)
- Quality: ROUGE-L, hallucination rate, classification accuracy
- Failure modes: common hallucination patterns and examples with recommended prompt fixes

Quality regression concerns / mitigations:
- We’ll run the full labeled set at start and end of the eval to detect regressions. If LlamaX shows a >3% drop in factuality vs Mistral, we flag it as regression and recommend fallback rules.
- Suggesting an automatic fallback policy: if confidence score < threshold OR hallucination heuristic triggers, route to LlamaX or to human review queue.

Benchmarks & artifacts:
- Benchmark summary (attached) — quick numbers for expected p95 and cost on Redwood Dedicated.
- Prompt set (attached) — canonical prompts + negative examples we plan to use for prompt tuning.
- Full eval dashboard will be shared at the end of Week 1 and Week 2.

Next steps (action items):
- Acme: share labeled set and confirm VPC requirement by Thu EOD.
- Redwood: provision Mistral-7B + LlamaX-13B eval lanes and share S3 links for logs + dashboard.
- Schedule 30-min sync: Thu 10:30am PST or Fri 11:00am PST — which works for you?

If that looks good I’ll get the eval ticket started today.

Best,
Marissa
